findings.text: The reviewed run's gate log does not carry the header its own manifest contract requires: 'a gate log's first line names the revision it ran at, the tree, and the command'. Its first line is the pytest session banner, and neither the revision nor the command appears anywhere in the log (only rootdir names the tree). The gate result is sound and reproduces, but a later reader cannot tie this log to a revision without outside context; this review's own arms (base-gate.log, head-gate.log) carry the header. Recorded so the next catalogue-shaped node emits a headed log, not as a defect of the change.

The catalogue declares probe_angle_source 'description', but binds no magnetics/b_field_pol_probe/angle and the converted store's magnetics.nc carries no probe angle (verified read-only via imas.DBEntry: b_field_pol_probe[0].angle is None), so read_geometry_table yields NaN probe angles. Plan section 4 defers the angle sense to section 6 and calls it 'marked unknown-unvalidated', yet the deferral is recorded only in a comment in tests/data/test_jt60sa_machine_map.py, not as a catalogue-level qualification (identity_qualifications is empty). Not a section-4 done-when failure, but a follow-on for the node that settles the angle sense.

follow_ons: probe_angle_source 'description' with no bound probe angle and no store angle leaves the directed probe angles NaN; section 6 is the node that settles their sense, and a catalogue-level qualification would make the deferral explicit rather than leaving it in a test comment.

The store writes empty pf_active coil-element names, so structure_assemblies' element_identifiers use a trailing-slash placeholder (jt60sa-op1-pf-active-cs1/element-0/); naming the elements in imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py would let the catalogue carry real element identifiers.
The reviewed run's gate log lacks a revision/tree/command header; the next node of this shape should emit the header the manifest contract names.
